title: How To Handle Students Who Do Nothing
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin tackles students who simply refuse to do any work, arguing the instinctive teacher response -- rushing over, pleading, prodding, and reteaching -- is both stressful and counterproductive because it rewards inaction with attention. Drawing an analogy to his own disciplined avoidance of digital distraction and embrace of boredom to force productive habits, he argues that the most effective response to a work-refusing student is to visibly withdraw concern entirely, letting the natural weight of incomplete work (lost grades, lost privileges, boredom itself) shift fully onto the student. He is explicit that this only works if the teacher has already taught a compelling, clearly understood lesson and eliminated any legitimate excuse for not knowing what to do, and that the strategy can take repeated attempts before a chronically rescued student learns that no one is coming to lighten their load.
points: Rushing to a work-refusing student with prodding, pleading, or reteaching is identified as ineffective and often rewards inaction with attention.
Withdraw visible concern entirely and let the natural consequences of not working (grades, privileges, boredom) shift the burden onto the student.
The strategy only works if the teacher has already taught a compelling lesson and eliminated any legitimate excuse for the student not knowing what to do.
For students used to being rescued, the lesson can take repeated attempts to sink in, but persistence eventually produces independent work habits.
quotes: So you rush over and ask what the problem is. You prod and push. You flatter and threaten. You counsel and kneel down to reteach.
Although counterintuitive—and blasphemy in the current educational milieu—the best thing you can do for them is let them be.
Simply allow the weight of not doing the assignment (i.e. its effect on grades, academic performance, skill acquisition, loss of recess, etc.) shift from burdening you to them.
For students unaccustomed to being left without the world rushing to lighten their accountability, it takes a while for the lesson to sink in. But sink in it will.
It puts them into a highly pleasurable flow state, where time distorts and contentment soothes. It raises their self-worth and provides a sense of real accomplishment.
